replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Design has profile update for logged-in user; IDOR/parameter substitution is a concrete attack on that endpoint."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Design states 30-day cookie sessions; no invalidation on contact change is a concrete, design-linked threat."},{"id":"T3","keep":true,"reason":"CSRF on the no-password settings endpoint with long-lived cookie is a distinct attack vector."},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Hijacked session escalating to permanent takeover via unverified instant email change; supported by quotes."},{"id":"T5","keep":false,"reason":"Same attack on email change endpoint with unverified instant change; duplicates T4's email-takeover threat.","duplicateOf":"T4"},{"id":"T6","keep":true,"reason":"Distinct harm: shipping address rewrite diverts physical goods, separate from email/account takeover."},{"id":"T7","keep":true,"reason":"No notification/audit of immediate email change named by design; distinct repudiation/detection gap."},{"id":"T8","keep":true,"reason":"Design serves a page rendering email, phone, address; caching of that document is specific."},{"id":"T9","keep":true,"reason":"Phone field change hijacks SMS recovery — different field, different recovery path harm than email takeover."}]}
